business_problem: Sanofi needed to speed and improve early biologics and mRNA vaccine discovery, where scientists must search enormous candidate spaces, design complex multi-target molecules, improve oral biologic stability, and predict vaccine performance and patient responses earlier in R&D.
solution_summary: Sanofi describes an in-house AI stack embedded across early R&D for biologics and mRNA vaccines. In biologics discovery, teams use AI and machine learning to screen large virtual panels, refine molecule designs in silico, and support target selection and engineering of complex trispecific antibodies for HIV and cancer. For mRNA work, Sanofi built CodonBERT, a large language model trained on millions of sequences, and mRNA-LM for full-length mRNA sequence modeling, to explore the vast design space and select promising vaccine sequences. RiboNN adds a deep-learning layer that predicts how efficiently ribosomes translate mRNA into protein. The company says these models are backed by deliberate experimental data generation and internal data infrastructure so the right biological data is produced, made available, and reused for model building. Scientists consume the model outputs to optimize efficacy, manufacturability, oral stability, and early response prediction, while the BioAIM program industrializes AI usage across the biologics portfolio.

solution_components.name: CodonBERT
solution_components.role: A large language model for mRNA that Sanofi uses to model sequence patterns and help design vaccine candidates.

solution_components.name: mRNA-LM
solution_components.role: An extension model for full-length mRNA sequences used to evaluate and design complete vaccine sequences.

solution_components.name: RiboNN
solution_components.role: A deep learning model that predicts how efficiently ribosomes will translate an mRNA sequence into a protein.

data_flow: Sanofi feeds large mRNA sequence collections, experimental data, and early biological signals into in-house models including CodonBERT, mRNA-LM, and RiboNN. These models score, generate, and refine candidate biologics and vaccine sequences in silico, and scientists use the outputs to choose targets, optimize molecule properties, improve manufacturability, and predict responses earlier in development.
business_outcome: Sanofi reports faster and more precise biologics and vaccine discovery, broader use of AI across its portfolio, improved ability to optimize efficacy and manufacturing efficiency, and shorter R&D cycles that help move treatments and vaccines toward patients sooner.
